Charbel: Lebanese Maronite form of Syriac Sharbel, after Saint Charbel Makhlouf. Possibly 'story of God' from Syriac; meaning not fully certain.
Illan: Probably a variant of Ilan, Hebrew 'tree', or of Irish Illann. Popular in France; origin partly uncertain.
Loay: Arabic Luay, meaning 'young bull' or 'strong'. Also the name of an ancestor of the Prophet's tribe.
Maximus: Latin, 'greatest'. A Roman cognomen borne by several saints and emperors.
Tian: Probably Chinese 'sky, heaven', or a short form of Christian or Sebastian in Europe. Origin varies.
Toots: Nickname of English origin, an affectionate pet name. As a given name probably a modern nickname; origin uncertain.
Jaylen: Modern American coinage, a blend of Jay and the suffix -len, as in Jalen. Meaning not fixed.
Mel: Short form of Melanie, Melissa or Melvin. Melanie is from Greek 'black, dark'.
Salimatou: West African form of Salima, from Arabic 'safe, sound'. The -tou ending is common among Fula and Mande speakers.
Ashanti: From the Ashanti people of Ghana, whose name probably means 'because of war'. Used as a given name in the African diaspora.
Darian: Variant of Darius, from Persian Dariush, 'holding firm the good'. Also a Spanish and English given name.
Shayan: Persian, meaning 'worthy, suitable'. Used in Iran and South Asia.
Syed: Arabic Sayyid, 'lord, master'. A title for descendants of the Prophet, used as a first name in South Asia.
Emanuele: Italian form of Emmanuel, Hebrew Immanuel, 'God is with us'.
Houd: Arabic Hud, a prophet in the Quran sent to the people of Ad. Possibly also from Hebrew, 'majesty'.
Tariq: Arabic, 'morning star' or 'one who knocks at the door'. Borne by the general Tariq ibn Ziyad.
Jinan: Arabic, meaning 'gardens' or 'paradise'. Also used in Syrian Arabic as a girls' name.
Louwis: Variant spelling of Lewis or Louis, from Germanic Chlodovech, 'famous warrior'.
Nidal: Arabic, meaning 'struggle' or 'fight'. Used for boys and sometimes girls.
Roukaya: Arabic Ruqayya, meaning 'charm' or 'rising'. A daughter of the Prophet Muhammad.
Arturo: Italian and Spanish form of Arthur, possibly from Celtic 'bear' or from Roman Artorius.
Dre: Short form of Andre or Andrew, from Greek andreios 'manly'. Also a hip-hop nickname after Dr. Dre.
Faisal: Arabic, meaning 'decisive' or 'judge'. Borne by Saudi and Iraqi kings.
Joumana: Arabic Jumana, 'silver pearl'. A name popular in Lebanon and Syria.
Rihana: Arabic Rayhana, 'sweet basil' or 'fragrant plant'. Also spelled Rihanna.
Santo: Italian and Spanish, meaning 'holy, saint'. Also a surname.
Julianna: Feminine form of Julian, from Latin Julianus, from the Roman family Julius.
Rhys: Welsh, meaning 'ardour' or 'enthusiasm'. Borne by medieval Welsh princes.
Solomon: Hebrew Shlomo, from shalom 'peace'. The biblical king noted for wisdom.
Ioanna: Greek and Romanian feminine form of John, Hebrew 'God is gracious'.
Maimouna: Arabic Maymuna, 'blessed' or 'fortunate'. Common in West Africa.
Nathaniël: Greek form of Hebrew Netanel, 'God has given'. A biblical apostle.
Yaser: Arabic Yasir, 'easy' or 'well-off'. Variant spelling of Yasser.
Abigael: Variant of Abigail, from Hebrew Avigayil, 'my father is joy'.
Violetta: Italian and Latin form of Violet, a diminutive meaning 'little violet' flower.
Ayyoub: Arabic Ayyub, form of Job. In Arabic possibly 'one who returns to God'.
Cyrus: Latinised Greek Kyros, from Persian Kurush, of uncertain meaning, possibly 'sun'. The Persian emperor.
Hina: Urdu, from henna, the plant dye. Also Japanese 'chick, doll' or 'sunlight'.
Ignacy: Polish form of Ignatius, from Latin Ignatius, probably 'fiery' or from Etruscan Egnatius.
Lie: Probably Dutch or Flemish short form of Liesbeth or Eliane, or Chinese Li. Origin uncertain.
Al: Short form of Albert, Alan, Alexander or Alfred. Germanic 'noble' in Albert's case.
Blue: English colour word used as a modern given name. A recent coinage.
Ecaterina: Romanian form of Catherine, from Greek aikaterine, possibly 'pure'.
Fer: Probably a short form of Fernando or Ferdinand, from Germanic 'bold journey'. Origin uncertain.
Julienne: French feminine of Julien, from Latin Julianus. Also the name of a vegetable cut.
Kingsley: English surname from Old English meaning 'king's wood or clearing'. Used as a first name, notably in Nigeria.
Amer: Arabic Amir or Amer, meaning 'prosperous' or 'long-lived'. Also Bosnian.
Frits: Dutch short form of Frederik, from Germanic 'peace ruler'.
Sooi: Possibly a Dutch variant of Sophie or a Frisian nickname. Origin uncertain.
Yunes: Arabic Yunus, the Quranic form of Jonah, from Hebrew yonah, 'dove'.
Anna-Lou: Compound of Anna, Hebrew 'grace', and Lou, a short form of Louise, 'famous warrior'.
Chase: English, from the surname meaning 'hunter' or 'hunt'. Used as a modern given name.
Tea: Probably a short form of Dorothea or Theodora, Greek 'gift of God'. Also Croatian and Finnish name; also English word for the drink.
Andra: Romanian feminine of Andrei, or short form of Alexandra and Andrea, from Greek 'manly, brave'.
Haniya: Arabic Haniyya, meaning 'happy, delighted'. Variant of Hania.
Pharrell: Of uncertain origin, popularised by musician Pharrell Williams. Possibly a variant of Farrell, Irish 'valour'.
Ambra: Italian, 'amber', from Arabic anbar. Also used in Italian for the fragrant ambergris.
Lauris: Latvian form of Laurence, from Latin Laurentius, 'from Laurentum', often linked to laurel.
Naia: Hawaiian 'dolphin', or a Greek variant of Naiad, a water nymph. Also a Basque name.
Osama: Arabic Usama, meaning 'lion'. A Companion of the Prophet bore it.
Annelou: Dutch compound of Anna and Lou, a short form of Louise. Anna is Hebrew 'grace'.
Evelin: Variant of Evelyn, from Norman French Aveline, probably Germanic 'hazelnut'. Also Hungarian and Estonian use.
Milad: Arabic and Persian, meaning 'birth, nativity'. Used in Iran and the Arab world.
Raissa: Russian Raisa, from Greek 'easy-going', or Arabic Raisa 'leader'. Also French Raïssa.
Abubakar: Arabic Abu Bakr, 'father of the young camel'. The first caliph.
Alhassane: Arabic Al-Hasan, 'the handsome, the good'. Common in West Africa.
Elizio: Variant of Elysio, from Latin Elysius, 'Elysian', or an Italian-style modern coinage. Origin uncertain.
Ferran: Catalan form of Ferdinand, from Germanic 'bold journey'. Also seen in Spanish use.
Firdaus: Arabic, 'paradise'. In Islam the highest level of Paradise.
Nalya: Probably a modern coinage or from Arabic Nalya. Possibly Slavic Natalya variant. Origin uncertain.
Lizz: Short form of Elizabeth, from Hebrew 'my God is an oath'.
Vasile: Romanian form of Basil, from Greek basileus, 'king'.
Ansar: Arabic, 'helpers'. Refers to the people of Medina who helped the Prophet.
Dima: Arabic 'downpour, steady rain', or Russian short form of Dmitri, from Demeter. Dual use.
Inti: Quechua, meaning 'sun'. The Inca sun god.
Lucius: Latin, from lux 'light'. Roman first name borne by several popes.
Oda: Germanic, from aud 'wealth, fortune'. Common in Norway and Germany.
Vicente: Spanish and Portuguese form of Vincent, from Latin vincens, 'conquering'.
Calie: Probably a variant of Callie or Kallie, from Greek kalos 'beautiful' or a Calista short form. Origin uncertain.
Esraa: Arabic Isra, meaning 'night journey'. After the Prophet's miraculous night journey.
Gisele: French form of Gisela, from Germanic gisil 'pledge, hostage'.
Fia: Scandinavian short form of Sofia, from Greek 'wisdom'. Also Scottish 'deer'.
Lazar: Slavic and Hebrew form of Lazarus, from Eleazar, 'God has helped'.
Mouhammad: Spelling of Muhammad, Arabic 'praised, highly commendable'.
Souhaïl: Arabic Suhayl, the star Canopus, meaning 'smooth, easy'.
Viënna: Dutch spelling of Vienna, the Austrian capital, from Celtic Vindobona.
Brenn: Probably a short form of Brennan, Irish 'sorrow' or 'raven', or Celtic Brennus. Origin uncertain.
Aiyana: Native American in style, said to mean 'eternal blossom'. Possibly Hindi or Sanskrit-influenced; origin uncertain.
Aye: Burmese, meaning 'cool' or 'peaceful'. Also an English word. Origin varies by use.
Haider: Arabic Haydar, 'lion'. A name of the fourth caliph Ali.
Yamen: Arabic Yamin, 'right hand' and 'blessing', or from Yemen, 'south'. Used for boys.
Callie: English short form of Caroline or Calista, or from Greek kalos 'beautiful'.
Klaus: German short form of Nikolaus, from Greek 'victory of the people'.
Meir: Hebrew, 'one who shines' or 'illuminator'. A rabbi of the Talmud bore it.
Miracle: English word name, from Latin miraculum, 'wonder'. Common in Nigeria.
Aarav: Sanskrit, meaning 'peaceful' or 'melodious'. Used in India.
Adelia: Latinised form of Adela, from Germanic adal, 'noble'.
Anabia: Probably Arabic-based, from Anbiya, or a variant of Anabella. Origin uncertain.
Aybüke: Turkish, from ay 'moon' and büke 'ornament'. A girls' name.
Cassius: Latin, from the Roman family name Cassius, possibly 'empty, hollow'. Muhammad Ali was born Cassius Clay.
Cilia: Probably a short form of Cecilia, from Latin Caecilius, possibly 'blind'. Also Latin 'eyelash'. Origin uncertain.
Dinis: Portuguese form of Denis, from Greek Dionysios, follower of Dionysus.
Ila: Sanskrit, 'earth' or 'speech'. Also a Polynesian name and a short Italian name.
Loui: Variant of Louis, from Germanic Chlodovech, 'famous warrior'.
Mazen: Arabic, meaning 'rain clouds' or 'carrying rain'. A male name.
Sig: Short form of names beginning with Sig-, from Germanic sigu 'victory'.
Amy-Lee: Compound of Amy, from French aimée 'beloved', and Lee, an English surname 'meadow'.
Isia: Probably a form of Isa or Isis, or Polish variant of Izabela. Origin uncertain.
Ouweys: Arabic Uways, a diminutive of aws 'gift' or 'wolf'. Associated with Uways al-Qarani.
Suleiman: Arabic form of Solomon, from Hebrew Shlomo, 'peace'.
Émeline: French diminutive of Emma, from Germanic ermen 'whole, universal'.
Fender: English surname from 'felt-maker' or 'defender'. As a given name probably after Fender guitars; modern coinage.
Jessim: Variant of Arabic Jassim, 'big, bulky', or Jasim. Origin uncertain.
Liara: Probably a modern coinage, perhaps from Lia and Ara, or Irish. Also a Mass Effect character name. Origin uncertain.
Linh: Vietnamese, meaning 'spirit' or 'soul'. Used for both sexes.
Mahsa: Persian, meaning 'like the moon'. Popular in Iran.
Manéo: Modern coined name, probably from Manu or Maël and Leo. Origin uncertain.
Maybel: English variant of Mabel, from Latin amabilis, 'lovable'.
Safiyya: Arabic, 'pure, sincere friend'. One of the Prophet's wives.
Willa: English feminine of William, from Germanic 'resolute protection'.
Amaani: Arabic Amani, 'wishes, hopes'. Plural of umniyya.
Hamidou: West African form of Arabic Hamid, 'praiseworthy'. The -ou ending is common in francophone Africa.
Minel: Probably Turkish Minel, from Arabic or from min 'small'. Origin uncertain.
Vladislav: Slavic, from vladeti 'to rule' and slava 'glory'.
Ghalia: Arabic Ghaliya, meaning 'precious, dear' or a fragrant perfume.
Lenora: Variant of Eleanor or Leonora, possibly from Greek 'light' or Provençal Alienor. Origin disputed.
Mathia: Probably a variant of Mathias or Matthias, from Hebrew 'gift of God'.
Mihaela: Romanian and Slavic feminine of Michael, Hebrew 'who is like God?'.
Adelio: Italian masculine of Adela, from Germanic adal, 'noble'.
Goldy: English pet name from gold, or Yiddish Golda, 'gold'. Also a nickname.
Olyvia: Variant spelling of Olivia, probably from Latin oliva, 'olive'.
Rahil: Arabic, meaning 'traveller, departing'. Also Hebrew-style Rahil from Rachel, 'ewe'.
Reyan: Arabic Rayyan, 'lush, well-watered'. Also the name of a gate of Paradise.
Silia: Possibly a short form of Cecilia or Silvia, or Latin Silius. Origin uncertain.
Valério: Portuguese form of Valerius, from Latin valere, 'to be strong'.
Azaan: Arabic Adhan, 'call to prayer'. Variant Azan.
Zuleyha: Turkish form of Zulaykha, in Islamic tradition the wife of Joseph. Possibly 'bright, brilliant'.
Carlota: Spanish and Portuguese form of Charlotte, feminine of Charles, from Germanic karl 'free man'.
Elanor: From Tolkien's Lord of the Rings, a golden flower, meaning 'sun-star' in Elvish. Also a variant of Eleanor.
Ella-Rose: English compound of Ella, from Germanic 'all' or 'other', and Rose, 'rose flower'.
Lysandro: Spanish and Italian form of Lysander, from Greek 'liberator of men'.
Odille: French form of Odila, from Germanic aud 'wealth'. Saint Odile is the patron of Alsace.
Taline: Armenian, probably meaning 'to give'. Also a modern coinage; origin partly uncertain.
Yasna: Slavic, 'clear, bright'. Also Avestan yasna, 'worship, sacrifice'.
Avery: English, from Norman Aubrey, Germanic Alberic, 'elf ruler'. Now used for both sexes.
Fernand: French form of Ferdinand, from Germanic 'bold journey'.
Joury: Arabic Jouri, 'red rose'. A name from Damascus rose heritage.
Nami: Japanese, 'wave'. Also a Korean 'little girl' or Arabic variant.
Ramata: West African, from Arabic Rahma, 'mercy'. Common in Mali and Senegal.
Sumeja: Bosnian, from Arabic Sumayya, 'high, exalted'. Name of the first martyr in Islam.
Timaé: Probably a modern French coinage or from Greek Timaios, 'honoured, valued'. Origin uncertain.
Aminatou: West African form of Aminata, from Arabic Amina, 'trustworthy, faithful'.
Aveline: Norman French diminutive of Avila or Ava, probably Germanic 'hazelnut'. Also Evelyn variant.
Hinata: Japanese, 'sunny place' or 'toward the sun'. Used for girls and boys.
Soléa: Probably a modern name from Spanish or Latin sol 'sun' or from soleil. Origin uncertain.
Leora: Hebrew, meaning 'light is mine'. Also a variant of Eleanor.
Loki: Norse, the trickster god. Probably 'knot' or 'closer', origin uncertain. Modern Marvel-influenced name.
Léonel: French and Spanish form of Lionel, a diminutive of Léon, 'lion'.
Massilia: Latin name for Marseille, from Greek Massalia. Also Berber-style rarer name. Origin uncertain.
Noxx: Modern coined name, probably from Latin nox 'night'. Origin uncertain.
Riff: English word for a repeated musical phrase. Probably a modern coinage or Dutch nickname.
Aksil: Amazigh (Berber), meaning 'leopard' or 'panther'. Common in Kabylie.
Juneyd: Turkish form of Arabic Junayd, 'little soldier'. Name of a Sufi saint.
Rokhaya: Senegalese form of Arabic Ruqayya, 'charm' or 'rising'.
Sylvester: Latin Silvestris, 'of the forest'. Name of several popes.
Daniyal: Arabic and Persian form of Daniel, Hebrew 'God is my judge'.
Everly: English surname meaning 'boar clearing', from Old English. Now a modern girls' name.
Harrie: Dutch short form of Hendrik or Harry, from Henry, Germanic 'home ruler'.
Kayan: Probably Persian-style, 'noble' or 'king', or Turkish. Also an ethnic group in Borneo. Origin uncertain.
Lessio: Probably a variant of Alessio, Italian form of Alexis, Greek 'defender'. Origin partly uncertain.
Léanore: Variant of Eleanor or Leonora, probably Provençal or Greek 'light'. Origin disputed.
Nayara: Possibly Basque or Brazilian Tupi origin. Meaning uncertain; sometimes linked to 'Naira'.
Rey: Spanish, 'king'. Also a short form of Reynaldo or Reyna.
Sianna: Probably a variant of Siana or Sienna, from the Italian city of Siena. Also an Irish Sinéad variant. Origin uncertain.
Zoha: Arabic Duha, 'forenoon' or 'morning light'. Also spelled Zuha.
Anette: Scandinavian and German form of Annette, a diminutive of Anna, Hebrew 'grace'.
Djena: Probably a variant of Jenna or Djenna, from Arabic Janna, 'paradise'. Origin uncertain.
Kahil: Arabic Kahil or Khalil, meaning 'close friend', or from Kahlil. Origin partly uncertain.
Manha: Possibly Arabic Minha, 'gift, grant'. Also a Korean name. Origin uncertain.
Ceder: Dutch word for the cedar tree, from Greek kedros. Modern given name.
Eloisa: Spanish and Italian form of Heloise, from Germanic Helewidis, possibly 'healthy, wide'.
Genesis: Greek, 'origin, creation'. Title of the first book of the Bible.
Julo: Probably a short form of Julius or Julian, from Latin. Also a Dutch nickname. Origin uncertain.
Stelle: Probably from Latin stella 'star' or a variant of Estelle. Origin uncertain.
Toto: Italian and Spanish pet name, for Salvatore or Antonio. Also the African musical group name; origin varies.
